@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
+# Victual 0.4.4
+
+**Tag `v0.4.4`, on `master` at the commit that merges this record.** It follows
+[0.4.3](0.4.3.md).
+
+## What changed
+
+| Change | Effect for an operator or client |
+|---|---|
+| Renderer claim ticks signal `db-changed-time` when they reap or claim work ([PR 973](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/pull/973), issue 898). | Clients can refresh after a claim tick changes visible state. Empty polls remain no-ops, and the response contract is unchanged. |
+| Artifact storage and preview collection are serialized ([PR 972](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/pull/972), issue 926). | Concurrent collection cannot remove an artifact while its storage operation is completing. |
+| Published artifact references for 0.4.3 were added to its release record ([PR 971](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/pull/971)). | Documentation only; no runtime effect. |
+
+The release adds no database migration, permission, configuration, or deployment-path
+change. It preserves response shapes and accepted inputs.
+
+## Verified before the tag
+
+| Check | Result | Reproduce |
+|---|---|---|
+| Version copies, chart render, OpenAPI and CI helpers after the version update | pending | `python3 .devtools/ci/release_version.py --check`; `python3 .devtools/ci/render_k3s.py --check`; `python3 .devtools/ci/check_openapi_document.py victual.openapi.json`; `python3 -m unittest discover -s .devtools/ci` |
+| Upgrade from `v0.4.3` over a populated database | No migration files changed since `v0.4.3`; no schema upgrade is required. A populated-database rehearsal was not run for this release. | Compare `db/` migration files with the `v0.4.3` tag; `.devtools/pgsql/upgrade-rehearsal/rehearse.sh` covers the project's fixed historical upgrade path. |
+| `tests` workflow, suite-floor and frontend-security | Passed on PR #973 head tree `c80b3d3bb72b581dbdcd6a6f3c11534e91b31d56`; the merged tree is identical. | [tests workflow](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/actions/runs/38828409695) |
+| Psalm security scan and prose checks | Passed on PR #973 head tree; the merged tree is identical. | [Psalm](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/actions/runs/38828409764); [prose](https://github.com/datagen24/victual/actions/runs/38828409689) |
+| Focused claim tick tests | Passed locally with PostgreSQL 16: `labeltracking` (4 tests/18 assertions), `labelservices` (310/1,945), and `labelapi` (177/4,827). | `.devtools/pgsql/run-tests.sh labeltracking`; `.devtools/pgsql/run-tests.sh labelservices`; `.devtools/pgsql/run-tests.sh labelapi` |
+| Production images and Helm chart publication | Pending signed tag and release workflow. | `.github/workflows/release.yml` |

@@ -3,7 +3,7 @@ "info": { "title": "Victual REST API", "description": "Authentication uses one of the credentials below. Which one is accepted depends on the operation.

**API key.** Send an API key you manage [here](PlaceHolderManageApiKeysUrl) in the *VICTUAL-API-KEY* header. Add the optional *VICTUAL-API-KEY-TYPE* header to narrow which key types may match; it can only remove authority, never add it. A read-only key is limited to GET, HEAD and OPTIONS and gets **403** on anything else; it also gets **403** on three GET operations that write: GET /calendar/ical/sharing-link, GET /stock/barcodes/external-lookup/{barcode} and GET /print/shoppinglist/thermal. A general API key is never accepted in the query string; the calendar secret on GET /calendar/ical is the only query-string credential.

**Session cookie.** Requests from the frontend authenticate with the *victual_session* cookie. On API routes, a request authenticated by the session cookie other than GET, HEAD or OPTIONS is refused with **403** when its Origin header (or its Referer header, if there is no Origin) names another origin. A request with neither header is allowed. Requests authenticated by an API key rather than the session cookie are exempt.

**Calendar secret.** The calendar feed link carries a calendar key in the *secret* query parameter. It is accepted on GET /calendar/ical only. GET /calendar/ical/sharing-link does not accept it, and no other operation does.

**Label worker, verifier and renderer keys.** These use the same *VICTUAL-API-KEY* header but are accepted only on the label worker and renderer operations that name them. On those operations user API keys, session cookies and a disabled-authentication setup are refused with **401**. POST /labels/pair is public.

**Deployment modes.** These are not credentials. With reverse-proxy authentication the server takes the user's identity from a header set by the proxy. In dev, demo and prerelease modes, in an embedded install, and with authentication disabled, requests run as the default user without a credential, except on the label worker and renderer operations above.

**Dates and times.** Every instant this API stores or sends is RFC 3339 in UTC with exactly six fractional digits - `2026-10-04T18:30:00.000000Z` - typed *format: date-time* (ADR-0027 decision 2, issue #650). The fixed width is part of the contract: text order is chronological order, so two values may be compared as strings. The one exception is *time_local* on the system time endpoint, the same instant with the server's offset (`2026-10-04T14:30:00.000000-04:00`). Fields whose column is a SQL DATE are calendar dates, typed *format: date* and written `YYYY-MM-DD`; they are never converted between zones. Days the server computes - due today, overdue, expiring in N days - are days in the server's configured time zone. A value sent without an offset - to the three write fields *tracked_time* and *done_time*, to a generic entity write, or as a `query[]` comparison - is a wall clock in the server's configured zone: a repeated hour names the earlier instant, and a skipped hour is refused with **400**. Send an offset to name any instant unambiguously. These values were local wall clocks in the server's zone, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, until migration 0301 converted them.

**Routing failures.** A path that matches no API route answers 404, and an unsupported method on a matched path answers 405. These routing outcomes are not listed on individual operations.
